question: How effectively do the existing rankings dismantle the original 2020 Energy and Minerals subnetwork?
population: Exactly the original case-study population: GraphML nodes with industry attribute Energy or Minerals; expect 112 nodes and 5075 directed edges.
scores: Reuse original DomiRank scores; degree and PageRank computed on the same binary induced graph. PageRank damping 0.85, uniform teleportation and dangling distribution, power-iteration L1 tolerance 1e-12.
primary_order: Fixed descending pre-removal scores. Reproduce the existing case script's min-max-scaled DomiRank sorting and GraphML insertion order for ties. No score or parameter updates after removal.
removal: Remove one node and all its incident edges at each step, from zero through all nodes. No edge-thresholding, reweighting or cascade rule.
primary_metric: Largest weakly connected component, retaining an edge irrespective of direction for connectivity. Report raw counts, fraction of original node count, and fraction of initial largest-component size.
secondary_metric: Largest strongly connected component, requiring directed mutual reachability; same normalizations.
summaries: Normalized trapezoidal area under each full removal curve; component counts after 10 and 20 removals; removals required to reach <=50% and <=10% of initial component size. Smaller values indicate faster dismantling.

random_reference.display: Mean and pointwise 2.5th–97.5th percentiles; random-order variability, not a confidence interval for model performance.

tie_sensitivity.rule: Randomly permute nodes within score groups tied at 12 decimal places after min-max scaling; retain score-group ordering.

sector_checks: Also report Energy and Minerals separately using the same original DomiRank scores restricted to each sector. Compute reference degree/PageRank on each evaluated graph. These prespecified secondary checks distinguish within-sector fragmentation from the allocation of removals between disconnected sectors.
verification: Reproduce case-study node/edge counts, saved top10 scores and Affective order, and all reported overlap counts. Verify saved ordinal ranks against tied-score rank intervals, recording order differences within ties. Independently verify deterministic component curves using Boolean transitive closure. Check monotonicity, endpoint counts, valid removal permutations, and unchanged input-file hashes.
